text:
If you’re looking for modern German cuisine in Berlin-Mitte, acht&dreissig is an excellent choice. Located directly on Oranienburger Straße, the restaurant combines traditional German dishes with contemporary techniques and creative presentation.

One of the highlights is the seasonal three-course menu, which offers great value for anyone wanting to experience the kitchen’s current creations. We decided to add an extra course, and it was absolutely worth it. The portions were surprisingly generous, making the menu both satisfying and well balanced.

The standout dish of the evening was the 24-hour slow-cooked pork belly. It was incredibly tender, rich in flavor, and beautifully prepared.

The restaurant also features a lovely outdoor terrace overlooking Oranienburger Straße, making it a wonderful place to enjoy dinner while watching the lively atmosphere of Berlin-Mitte.

The service was exceptionally friendly, attentive, and professional throughout the evening.

If you’re searching for a good modern German restaurants in Berlin-Mitte, or simply want to experience classic German cuisine with a contemporary twist, acht&dreissig is well worth a visit. We’ll definitely be back.

text:

The champagne reception with a flying buffet took place throughout the restaurant and on the terrace, the main course was served in the back at the open show kitchen, and dessert was beautifully presented at the bar. The front area was then used as a dance floor with a lounge corner and photo booth – the layout was simply ideal for our number of guests.

We would especially like to highlight the service. The entire team was incredibly attentive, warm, and professional all evening. We didn't have to worry about a thing and could simply enjoy our day. Our guests also repeatedly commented on how friendly and dedicated the whole team was.

A big thank you also goes to the restaurant management. They provided us with fantastic support during the preparations and put us in touch with Flora Werkstatt, who ultimately took care of our floral arrangements. That was a real stroke of luck!

The food was outstanding, the organization was seamless, and we felt completely at ease from our initial conversation to the end of the celebration.


We would also like to emphasize the service. Many thanks to the entire team for this unforgettable evening!

Judging the food itself, it was slightly disappointing by my standards.

We had a reservation for a larger group last weekend. Normally, and understandably, the restaurant has a policy of free cancellation up to a few days in advance, with a no-show fee applying afterwards.

Unfortunately, our group was faced with a medical emergency that dramatically changed our plans. After calling the restaurant and reaching out to the manager by phone and text, we were met with nothing but understanding from their side. They kindly agreed not to charge any cancellation fee.

While this may seem like the logical and humane thing to do in such a situation, it was still very much appreciated and one less thing to worry about during a difficult moment. That kind of understanding and flexibility says a lot about the management.

Very decent management right there! Next time we're in Berlin, this will be the first place we're going to.

text:
We closed out our four days in Berlin with another great dinner spot -- Acht & Dreissig.  This is another gem in the Mitte area of town.  The service is warm, efficient and helpful. They made us feel like it was OUR neighborhood restaurant.

The food was excellent too.  We tried their seasonal White Asparagus Soup.  It was devine.  Such a good taste of the featured vegetable, with wild garlic oil and a side of crusty bread.

For dinner we had the Braised Ox Cheek, which came with potato cream, carrots, broccoli and Port wine gravy.  Save some bread to get up every bit of gravy.  Our other entree was a filet of Perch with potatoes and white asparagus with hollandaise sauce.

Check out the menu online, it is small, but everything on it looks delicious.  I would recommend dinner on the patio, but the inside is also beautiful.

placeAddress: YOU. Berlin, Charlottenstraße 52, 10117 Berlin, Germany
text:
We had our wedding reception at Heritage last year. It was an absolutely perfect evening, superbly organized by Anna Sefrin and brilliantly executed by her team! I've already written a review about it.

As a tradition, we'll now eat here every year on our wedding anniversary. Yesterday was the first time. :-)

We had, of course, reserved a table in advance and were truly touched that they decorated our chosen table with paper hearts and invited us for a glass of Crémant upon arrival. I think that's really exceptional, especially these days. Everyone on the staff knew the reason for our visit and congratulated us. Just like last year, we immediately felt welcome and comfortable. Fantastic!

The food was, as expected, very good. Yes, a three-course meal is also expensive and perhaps borderline pricey, but in our opinion, the quality is commensurate.

The restaurant itself is beyond compare. For me, it's one of the most beautiful restaurants in Berlin and beyond!

The service is, in our opinion, perfectly balanced between the necessary courtesy one expects at this level and a very pleasant, understated informality. This creates a thoroughly comfortable atmosphere. Yes, as some have criticized, the staff aren't at our table every two minutes, but we don't need that. I prefer it this way to being constantly asked if we'd like another glass of wine, etc. Ultimately, it's a matter of taste, but for us, it works very well.

We enjoyed another wonderful evening at the Heritage and would therefore like to extend our sincere thanks to the service team, the chefs, and Anna.

By the way, anyone planning a family celebration at the Heritage should be in excellent hands with Anna Sefrin. She was one of the reasons we chose the Heritage as our wedding venue.
originalText:
Wir hatten letztes Jahr unser Hochzeitsessen im Heritage. Das war ein rundum perfekter Abend, top von Anna Sefrin organisiert und super umgesetzt von ihrem Team! Eine entsprechende Rezension hatte ich bereits geschrieben.

Als Tradition werden wir nun jedes Jahr an unserem Hochzeitstag hier essen gehen. Gestern war das erste Mal.  :-)

Wir hatten den Tisch natürlich vorher reserviert und waren wirklich gerührt, dass man uns unseren Wunschtisch mit Papierherzen dekoriert und uns zum Empfang auf ein Glas Crémant eingeladen hat. Ich finde gerade in der heutigen Zeit ist das wirklich außergewöhnlich. Jeder im Service wusste von dem Anlass unseres Besuchs und gratulierte uns. Wir haben uns, wie damals, sofort willkommen und wohl gefühlt. TOP!

Das Essen war wie erwartet sehr gut. Ja, es ist bei einem Drei-Gänge-Menü auch kostenintensiv und möglicherweise grenzwertig, hat jedoch auch die entsprechende Qualität, wie wir persönlich finden.

Die Räumlichkeiten sind über jeden Zweifel erhaben. Für mich eines der schönsten Restaurants in Berlin und darüber hinaus!

Der Service ist für unseren Geschmack perfekt ausbalanciert zwischen der notwendigen Höflichkeit, die man auf dem Niveau erwartet, und einer sehr angenehmen, nicht übertriebenen "Lockerheit". So entsteht für uns eine rundum wohlige Atmosphäre. Ja, die Mitarbeiter sind, wie manche kritisiert haben, nicht alle 2 Minuten am Tisch, aber wir brauchen das auch nicht. Das ist mir so lieber, als wenn man andauernd gefragt wird, ob man nicht doch noch ein Glas Wein etc. möchte. Am Ende Geschmacksache, für uns passt das sehr gut.

Wir haben erneut einen sehr schönen Abend im Heritage genossen und möchten uns daher auch beim Service-Team, den Köchen und Anna sehr herzlich bedanken.

Übrigens, wer mal eine Familienfeier im Heritage erleben möchte ist bei Anna Sefrin in besten Händen. Sie war einer der Gründe, warum wir uns damals als Hochzeitslocation für das Heritage entschieden haben.

text:
I wrote to the restaurant directly after my stay but unfortunately never received a reply. Therefore, here is my review.

Hello Heritage Team,

I gave my girlfriend a voucher for breakfast, which we redeemed this morning.

Even the greeting was impersonal and curt. The colleague who greeted me was unfriendly and annoyed throughout our entire stay, and her tone with her colleagues was inappropriate, especially when guests could hear it.

In a hotel of this caliber, the velvet furniture shouldn't have so many stains.

I researched the location thoroughly before choosing it and therefore expected a very good breakfast, which one would expect for €38.

Unfortunately, the breakfast did not meet our expectations.

The selection of egg dishes is good. We opted for the Eggs Benedict. However, the hollandaise sauce was curdled.

The bread selection is also good, but it's a shame that the pastries aren't homemade. Especially the cake!

It would be better to offer less, but make it all homemade.

The cheese selection was particularly disappointing!

No hard cheeses, sheep's cheese, or goat's cheese.

Consequently, the jams were pointless.

None of the spreads were homemade.

Liverwurst in plastic?

The only fish was salmon.

The fruit salad wasn't freshly made; the only freshly cut fruit was pineapple.

There were absolutely no highlights on the buffet.

In my opinion, coffee and tea should be served in a hotel of this price range, and even better would be if the coffee came from an espresso machine with hand-frothed milk.

Finally, the Crémant should be mentioned, which neither of us liked at all.

For a total of €100 for two people, it was a disappointing experience; we've eaten much better elsewhere.

What a shame.

placeAddress: Samurai Wagyu Yakiniku & Sushi Berlin Mitte, Hausvogteipl. 3-4, 10117 Berlin, Germany
text: I took a few days to let my impressions of Samurai (which isn't run by Japanese, but Vietnamese) sink in, in order to write a review based on rational core elements and leaving out emotional musings. However, the more I think about this two-hour culinary journey, the grayer the memories become, because it really was nothing more than an all-you-can-eat buffet. And that buffet costs €35.90 per person (drinks not included [at least one must be ordered]). Customers have 120 minutes for this all-you-can-eat experience (10 rounds of 12 minutes each, with a maximum of 15 items per round). And yes, that's a lot, but the first items (rice, fries, miso soup, round meat, etc.) didn't arrive until 14 minutes in, effectively depriving the customer of an entire round. The staff seemed very rushed and tried to adhere to the tight two-hour schedule per table, even though after the meal the entire table grill had to be cleaned, customers instructed on the process, ingredients brought, and the bill prepared. This unfortunately created the impression that the customer was nothing more than an interchangeable variable, which I found very off-putting. Also problematic was the fact that the waiters and waitresses often didn't speak German, meaning certain questions couldn't be answered. Two hours might sound like a long time, but it creates a sense of urgency, and it was clear that many guests, especially in the first few minutes, were trying to cram in as much food as possible because of the time pressure. As for the atmosphere: it has a Japanese influence, but the traditional elements are subject to the typical Berlin tendency to force them into a modern and minimalist aesthetic, resulting in an extremely dark, almost claustrophobic atmosphere. The restaurant heats up so much from the countless table grills that just sitting there brings beads of sweat to your forehead, which is extremely unpleasant. As for the food, I can say it's good, but nothing more, and it doesn't particularly stand out. Unfortunately, it's obvious that the "Japanese" is a multi-Asian cuisine adapted to German palates, the kind you can find at practically every Asian restaurant in Berlin, except here the customer prepares the food themselves on the table grill, and the countless bowls and plates quickly turn the seating area into a battlefield. It's a nice little culinary experience, but it didn't leave a particularly memorable impression.
originalText: Ich habe mir ein paar Tage Zeit genommen, meine Eindrücke über das Samurai (welches nicht von Japanern betrieben wird, sondern von Vietnamesen) sacken zu lassen, um eine Review zu verfassen, welche sich auf rationale Kernelemente stützt und emotionales Geplänkel außen vorlässt, doch je mehr ich über diese zweistündige kulinarische Reise nachdenke, desto grauer werden die Erinnerungen, denn mehr als ein All-you-can-eat-Buffet war es dann doch nicht. Und jenes schlägt mit 35,90€ pro Person zu Buche (Getränke exkl. [Eines muss mindestens bestellt werden]). Für jenes All-you-can-eat-Erlebnis stehen dem Kunden 120 Minuten zur Verfügung (10 Runden à 12 Minuten mit jeweils max. 15 Items). Und ja, das ist viel, jedoch kamen die ersten Items (Reis, Pommes, Miso-Suppe, Rundfleisch etc.) erst nach 14 Minuten an, wodurch sozusagen der Kunde einer ganzen Runde beraubt wurde. Das Personal wirkt sehr gehetzt und versucht, die enge Taktung von 2h/Tisch einzuhalten, auch wenn nach dem Essen der gesamte Tischgrill gereinigt werden muss, die Kunden in den Prozess eingewiesen werden müssen, die Zutaten gebracht, und die Rechnung erstellt werden muss. Und hier entsteht fatalerweise der Eindruck, dass man als Kunde nicht mehr als eine austauschbare Variable ist, und dies stieß mir sehr negativ auf, auch, dass die Kellner/innen häufig nicht der deutschen Sprache mächtig sind und so bestimmte Fragen nicht geklärt werden konnten. Zwei Stunden mögen viel klingen, doch sie erzeugen Zeitdruck, und bei vielen Gästen war erkennbar, dass sie vor allem in den ersten Minuten bemüht waren, so viel wie möglich Nahrung in sich hineinzustopfen, da die Zeit im Nacken liegt. Von der Atmosphäre kann so viel gesagt werden: Sie ist japanisch angehaucht, jedoch unterliegt das Traditionelle der typischen Berliner Affinität, jenes in die Moderne und den Minimalismus zu zwingen, woraus eine überaus dunkle, beinahe klaustrophobische Atmosphäre entsteht. Auch wärmt sich das Lokal durch die unzähligen Tisch-Grille dermaßen auf, dass allein das Sitzen bereits Schweißperlen auf die Stirn zaubert, und dies ist äußerst unangenehm. Von der Speisequalität kann ich berichten, dass sie gut ist, aber mehr nicht, und sie sticht auch nicht besonders hervor, und leider merkt man, dass das „Japanische“ eine an den deutschen Gaumen angepasste multiasiatische Küche ist, welche so bei eigentlich jedem Berliner Asiaten zu finden ist, nur dass hier der Kunde die Nahrungsmittel selbst am Tischgrill zubereitet und durch die unzähligen Schüsseln und Teller der Sitzplatz alsbald einem Schlachtfeld gleicht. Es ist ein nettes und kleines kulinarisches Erlebnis, jedoch blieb es bei mir nicht als besonders einzigartig im Gedächtnis.

Two minor criticisms:

Finally getting to our table, we received a menu after 20 minutes and were only able to order after 45 minutes. Until then, there were no drinks... no bread... and when we ordered, the server rattled off the menu... among other things, we ordered the unlimited water for the table. After the food and drinks were finally delivered, we were completely ignored by the staff. No one asked if we wanted more water; you had to be quite forceful to even get eye contact.

We booked the 36 Rooms Hostel Kreuzberg Berlin for July 4th. Upon arrival, however, the staff informed us that we could only check in or enter the hostel with a passport. When we questioned this, they claimed that this requirement was clearly stated on Hostelworld—which was completely untrue.

This condition was not clearly disclosed during the booking process, and it is unacceptable to impose such a rule on guests upon arrival after a reservation has already been made. This seemed misleading, dishonest, and extremely unprofessional.

Our experience was very disappointing, and we did not feel that the hostel had treated us transparently or fairly. I strongly advise future guests to be very careful and to check everything thoroughly before booking.

placeAddress: Pizzeria Piccola Musica Berlin, Wiener Str. 62, 10999 Berlin, Germany
text:
I ordered from this takeaway—that's all it is in my opinion—on Friday, October 16, 2020, via a delivery app.

The pizza arrived lukewarm and was neither Italian nor American. It was more like a sheet of dough without a crispy crust. Also, if you're going to list beef salami, you should probably mention that the salami is spicy.

For a starter, I had garlic soup. The soup was extremely salty and tasted more like a garlic cream sauce. I couldn't find any fresh garlic. When ordering soup from a restaurant, as the name suggests, I expect bread. The bread wasn't mentioned in the description, so it doesn't really matter.

The delivery was estimated at 90 minutes and arrived after 75. On a Friday evening, that would be acceptable if the pizza had been properly piping hot. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone.
originalText:
Habe bei dem Imbiss mehr ist es in meinen Augen nicht, am Freitag 16.10.2020 bestellt über eine Lieferapp.

Die Pizza kam lauwarm an und war weder italienisch noch amerikanisch. Sie war mehr ein Teiglappen ohne knusprige Kruste. Außerdem sollte man wenn man schon Rindersalami schreibt vielleicht erwähnen das die Salami dazu noch scharf ist.

Zur Vorspeise hatte ich eine Knoblauchsuppe. Die Suppe war extrem versalzen und erinnerte ehr an eine Knoblauchsahne Soße. Frischen Knoblauch suchte ich vergebens. Zu einer Suppe wünsche ich mir bei einem Restaurant wie es im Namen heißt auch Brot. Das Brot stand in der Beschreibung nicht drin von daher auch egal.

Die Lieferung war mit 90min angegeben und kam nach 75min.
Am Freitag Abend ist das in Ordnung wenn die Pizza auch noch richtig warm gewesen wäre. Empfehle ich niemandem den Laden.
